fact: LIBTELCO's managing director said its mandate to provide ICT services to government is enshrined in the Telecommunications Act of 2007 and the National Telecommunications and ICT policy, so the policy was in force; dated to the article's published date, as it gives none.

The strategy states that a new national ICT policy (2025-2029, elsewhere 2025-2030) has been drafted and is undergoing consultation for approval and adoption, with validation of the draft ongoing and approval targeted for Q4 2025; the document gives no date for this status, so the document's published date is used.
The draft successor policy is named 'ICT policy 2025 - 2030' in the strategy's initiatives and targets, though the background chapter calls it 2025-2029; the document's published date is used.

The strategy states that the Liberia ICT Policy (2019-2024) was adopted as part of the government's digitization efforts, built on three pillars (Structure, Empower, Transform); no adoption date is given, so the document's published date is used.
The strategy gives the Liberia ICT Policy's period as 2019-2024 and reviews its initiatives in Appendix C; the document's published date is used.

The strategy states that the governance structures in the ICT Policy 2019-24 (a National ICT Governing Board, CIO and CIO Council, with MoPT as lead) were implemented, though their effectiveness needs improving; the document's published date is used.

Appendix C of the strategy reviews the status of initiatives from the National ICT Policy (2019-2024) and comments on progress, stating for example that the recommended targets have not been met, including 50% of clinics and hospitals with internet access; the passages shown cover only some objectives, and the document's published date is used.
The policy sets itself over the next five years, 2019 to 2024, with a mid-term review at year 3 and a long-term review in year 5.
The full policy text is held on the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications website (mopt.gov.lr), published 2019-10-31.
The policy carries a summary of measurable targets with timelines of years 1 to 5 after adoption, and no cost figures appear in the passages read.

The policy assigns the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications overall coordination, implementation, review and oversight, with the LTA, an ICT Governing Board, a cross-ministerial CIO Council and a CIO to the Presidency supporting.
The passages read tie the policy to no budget line; the Executive is said only to ensure resources are available to the requisite ministries.
The document states that the National ICT and Telecoms policy of 2010 was adopted by Cabinet under the Telecommunications Act of 2007, and that the 2019-2024 policy updates and amends it.
The policy states that in 2019 the government adopted the Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Policy (2019-2024), built on three pillars (Structure, Empower, Transform).
The policy states that the National ICT Policy (2019-2024) was extended to 2025; it names no successor ICT policy (document dated March 2026).

The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications text of the National ICT Policy 2025-2030 is a draft dated 7 January 2025, whose development process lists validation workshops to finalise it; the document is dated by its published date, 2025-01-07.
The draft policy covers 2025-2030, with targets timed 'By 2030'; date is the document's published date.
The draft policy text is held on the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications website (mopt.gov.lr); date is the document's published date.

The draft sets out a table of key action areas, measurable targets and timelines per objective (for example train 500,000 youth in digital skills and fund 500 startups by 2030) and a priority programme table for 2025-2028, with no costs stated; date is the document's published date.

The draft gives the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications the formulation, coordination and oversight of the policy, with a dedicated monitoring and evaluation unit within the Ministry and a proposed National ICT Governing Council; date is the document's published date.

The draft says the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning shall ensure budgeting for implementation and lists development partners as providers of support, but states no budget line or amount; date is the document's published date.
The draft lists the National Telecommunications and ICT Policy (2019-2024) as expired.
The World Bank assessment states that a new five-year ICT policy (2019-2024) was signed by the President in 2019.
The assessment names the policy as the Liberia ICT Policy (2019-2024).

The assessment reports that the policy has 13 objectives and sets targets, such as a 20 percent improvement in school internet access and at least one ICT course in all secondary schools, with no cost stated.

The assessment states there is no authoritative body to coordinate implementation of the National ICT Policy and that mandates among government actors are unclear, with the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications' coordination ability limited; the National ICT Governing Board and CIO Council exist. Dated by the document's published date, 2020-01-01.
